- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.7) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 5–10 days.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior 5-day avg), model often overshoots; apply downward correction of 3–8% for 3–7 days post-spike.
- If sentiment is negative (≤-0.5) and price is trending down, model frequently underestimates; add 1–4% upward bias for next 5–10 days.
- Model shows strong mean reversion bias: if 30-day forecast is >10% above recent 10-day average, adjust downward by 1–3% for next 7 days.
- When sentiment shifts from negative to positive (e.g., -0.5 → +0.7), model often lags; forecast should be adjusted upward by 1–5% for next 3–5 days.
- For 30-day horizon, if model forecast is >10% above true outcome in first 5 days, apply 2–5% downward correction for remaining 25 days.
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed (±0.3), model tends to overfit recent volatility; use 50% smoothing of recent 7-day average to reduce noise.
